proofs.text: In a temp git project with `greeting.py`, one spec holding a high-risk rule and one tagged test, run init at `tested` and verify the quick run exits 0, that `--record --commit` writes a record under `.purlin/records/greeting/` and the gate check exits 0. Raise to `recorded` and verify the gate check exits 1; commit a second record under the build identity, verify it is labelled `ci` and the gate check exits 0. Raise to `approved` and verify the gate check exits 1 naming `purlin:init --gate approved`; set one approver and verify it exits 1 again; write a signed approval and verify the commit is signed and the gate check exits 0. Walk both the python and the typescript fixture

rule_text: A project init set up walks the three gates: the quick run passes, a record the developer commits meets `tested`, raising to `recorded` refuses that record and accepts one the build identity committed, and `approved` refuses first an empty approver list and then a high-risk rule with no approval, until a signed approval is written
